entry.title: Few books in Iran's contemporary history have created as many supporters and…
entry.summary:
Source: @miladdokhanchi

Few books in Iran's contemporary history have created as many supporters and opponents as Jalal Al-e-Ahmad's "Weststruckness." Some consider it a manifesto of return to self. Others see it as the beginning of a great misunderstanding. Usually, such texts have been read far less than the talk and rumors surrounding them; perhaps before judging this book, we need to read it once carefully, historically, and critically. In the re-reading course of "Weststruckness," we are not just going to read the famous text of Jalal Al-e-Ahmad from beginning to end; we are going to place this book within the context of the history of contemporary Iranian thought. Dr. Milad Dokhanchi, PhD graduate in Cultural Studies and author of the book "Post-Islamism: Revisiting the Relationship between Politics and Religion in Iran," will lead these sessions. - Session Zero: Tuesday, July 21 (Free) - Main sessions: 4 sessions, starting Tuesday, July 28, at 5 PM, House of Poetry and Literature - Attendance at Session Zero is free; the rest require registration. - Registration and payment link: https://jivegi.school/products/Jalal-Al-e-Ahmad

entry.title: Ⓜ️ We don't have something called society in Iran; in Iran, we have a mass.…
entry.summary:
Source: @miladdokhanchi

Ⓜ️ We don't have something called society in Iran; in Iran, we have a mass. A mass is a collection of bodies; humans who live next to each other, react, get excited, and pass by each other, but don't necessarily dialogue with one another. But "society" is something beyond being next to each other; society means minds that connect, dialogue, disagree, bring arguments, and participate in the process of collective understanding. 🔰 Watch Milad Dokhanchi's conversation on Azad Media. shakmediaa 🛄 @zistboommedia || School of Humanities

entry.title: 🎥 War, People, and the Future of Iran 🔶 Conversation between Shervin…
entry.summary:
Source: @miladdokhanchi

🎥 War, People, and the Future of Iran 🔶 Conversation between Shervin Vakili, Mohammad Mehdi Ardabili, and Milad Dokhanchi 🔻Mohammad Mehdi Ardabili: The constant claim that "the Islamic Republic is on its way out" has given society a kind of foolishness. Just as the government must be held accountable for the events of Dey month, the society that supported the war must accept its responsibility. Whoever does not accept their responsibility will repeat it again. The solution is not in "warmongering," but in "civil resistance"; the force that existed in "Woman, Life, Freedom." 🔺Shervin Vakili: Those who believe Iran has become strong must answer why a part of the people became warmongers and were happy about it? If we seek a powerful Iran, it is created with the support of a powerful people, not in a situation where the government is at war with a large part of the people. For example, when the internet—which is a natural right of the people—is cut off for a long time, it means fear of the people, and such a situation means Iran is not strong. 🔻Milad Dokhanchi: Iran has won a great war, but many of our intellectuals don't see it. Our main issue should be society-building, and its responsibility lies with the intellectuals of the public sphere, because the people have remained at the level of a mass. In such a state, the people cannot resist either the government or colonialism. The duty of activists and intellectuals is to build and strengthen society to resist these two forces of domination. 🎞 Full video of this conversation on Azad YouTube: https://youtu.be/kkCHZvJoMSM ✅ At the beginning of this conversation, important explanations about the infrastructural problems faced by Azad and the requirements for continuing activities are provided. entry.title: 🔸️ "Narrative craft" (Ravayat-varzi) refers to the art of designing and…
entry.summary:
Source: @miladdokhanchi

🔸️ "Narrative craft" (Ravayat-varzi) refers to the art of designing and orally presenting an idea, experience, or story in the form of a coherent narrative in the public sphere. Narrative craft is a form of rhetoric; an attempt to express one's world, connect with others, convey experience, persuade, and even entertain the audience. 🔹️Narrative craft is not just public speaking, and its main difference from public speaking lies in its reliance on "narrative"; that is, turning an experience, issue, or idea into a narrative, living, and impactful form. ✳️ This social skill is now used in various fields: from education, media, and content production to social action, entrepreneurship, management, policy-making, cultural activity, idea presentation, teaching, negotiation, personal branding, and even everyday life. 🔰 In the 12-hour "Narrative Craft" workshop with Dr. Milad Dokhanchi, we will learn the basics and main components of narrative craft; from narrative structure and tension to performance, rhythm, and audience connection. 🔆 Then each participant will work on their own idea and, with the help of the group, rewrite and refine their narrative. At the end, the narratives will be performed on stage. 🗓 Tuesdays from May 26 ⏰️ 6 to 9 PM Registration: 🌐https://jivegi.school/products/Storytelling

entry.title: 📜 The contemporary history of Iran is not just a collection of events; it is…
entry.summary:
Source: @miladdokhanchi

📜 The contemporary history of Iran is not just a collection of events; it is a network of decisions and ruptures that still operate in our "now."♨️ From the Constitutional Revolution to the Islamic Revolution, we face a chain of causes and effects; narratives that remain incomplete without analysis.✴️ The semester course "Contemporary History of Iran" is an attempt to read history with an analytical and document-based approach; focusing on the why, how, and consequences of events.✳️ In this course, each week we review the path of history by watching video books and studying supplementary texts, and prepare for a discussion-oriented session; a place for questioning, analysis, and seeing the deeper layers of history.🔻 This is not a memory-based class; it is an exercise in building a historical perspective.✅ If you want your analysis of today's issues to be more precise and rooted, this course can be a serious starting point.🔸️ Semester course "Contemporary History of Iran"👤 Reza Mokhtari Isfahani🗓 Wednesdays⏰ 18:00 to 20:00💻 Online (Skyroom)📤 Registration:🌐 https://jivegi.school/products/HistoryofIran2026🔗 Baleh channel: https://ble.ir/jivedebate
